fixes.value: Flow chart headed Annex B.1, "The Building (Amendment) Regulations 2004: amendments to Regulation 6 and Parts A and C, transitional provisions", for the Local Authority Building Control – Building Notice Route. It asks in order: "Before 1 December 2004, has a building notice been given?", then "Before 1 December 2004, has a commencement notice been given?", then "Before 1 December 2004, has building work started?". A No answer at any step leads to "Building work is subject to the amendments to Regulation 6 and Parts A and C, and to the new Approved Documents A and C.", and Yes at all three leads to "Building work is subject to the provisions and Approved Documents applicable at the time the building notice was given*", with the note "* But individual new buildings started on or after 1 December 2004 are subject to the revised Parts A and C and to the new Approved Documents."

fixes.value: Flow chart headed Annex B.2, "The Building (Amendment) Regulations 2004: amendments to Regulation 6 and Parts A and C, transitional provisions", for the Local Authority Building Control – Full Plans Route. It asks "Before 1 December 2004, have full plans been deposited?" (No leads to work subject to the amendments to Regulation 6 and Parts A and C, and to the new Approved Documents). If Yes, it asks "Before 1 December 2004, has the local authority: passed the plans without conditions; or stated in writing that any conditions have been fully met?"; Yes leads to work subject to the provisions and Approved Document applicable at the time the full plans were deposited. rows: Exempt buildings and work. Adds new para 5A relating to which conservatories and porches the exemption at regulation 9(3)(b) applies
Information about ventilation. Adds a new provision requiring information about a building’s ventilation system and its maintenance to be given to the building owner.
Supervision of building work other than by local authorities. Adds to regulation 20AA to the list of regulations which do not apply where the building work is subject to an initial notice.

Mechanical ventilation air flow rate testing. A new provision requiring mechanical air flow rates to be tested in accordance with a procedure approved by the Secretary of State and a notice of results give to the local authority in a manner approved by the Secretary of State.
Commissioning. Adds a new provision requiring the commissioning of fixed systems for mechanical ventilation where the testing and adjustment of such systems in possible.

CO2 emission rate calculations. Adds a new provision requiring the local authority to be given, before work starts, the target CO2 emission rate for the building, the calculated rate for the building as designed and a list of specifications used for the calculation of the emission rates.
Contravention of certain regulations not to be an offence. Adds regulation 20AA to the list of regulations to which section 35 of the Building Act does not apply.
Electronic service of documents. Adds notices under regulations 20AA, 20D(2)and 20D(3) to those that may be given electronically to the local authority.

rows: Principles of charging scheme: overriding objective in determining charges Require a LA to estimate and fix their charges with the aim of achieving the overriding objective of ensuring that “taking one financial year with another” their income from charges as nearly as possible equates to the costs incurred of carrying out the chargeable functions and providing chargeable advice, ie to break even and achieve full cost recovery. A LA is also required to review their charges at the end of each financial year to ensure that this objective is achieved.

Overriding principle similar to regulations 5(1) and 5(4) of the 1998 Regulations. New accounting requirement, ie “taking one financial year with another” replaces “a continuous period of 3 years” in regulation 5(5) of the 1998 Regulations. New requirement to review charges annually. ‘Derogation’ principle relating to the full cost recovery requirement in regulation 5(2) of the 1998 Regulations has been revoked.

Principles of charging scheme: overriding objective in determining charges Require a LA to prepare and publish a financial statement, approved by a person with the necessary financial authority, not more than six months after the end of each financial year setting out the chargeable costs, income and any surplus income or deficit arising.

Similar requirement for annual financial statement was set out in regulation 5(6) of the 1998 Regulations. There is a new requirement for any surplus income or deficit to be set out in the financial statement, and for the statement to be signed by a person with the necessary financial authority.

Principles of charging scheme: overriding objective in determining charges Where a LA first introduces a charging scheme under the 2010 Regulations midway through the financial year, the LA is required to take account of any estimated surplus or deficit arising for that part of the year under the 1998 Regulations. Reference to “a financial year” is also defined.
sentences: In the introduction table, regulation 6(1)-(3) of the 2010 Regulations, on principles of charging scheme: overriding objective in determining charges, requires a LA to estimate and fix their charges with the aim of achieving the overriding objective of ensuring that “taking one financial year with another” their income from charges as nearly as possible equates to the costs incurred of carrying out the chargeable functions and providing chargeable advice, ie to break even and achieve full cost recovery, and to review their charges at the end of each financial year to ensure that this objective is achieved; the main changes from the 1998 Regulations are an overriding principle similar to regulations 5(1) and 5(4), a new accounting requirement where “taking one financial year with another” replaces “a continuous period of 3 years” in regulation 5(5), a new requirement to review charges annually, and the revoking of the ‘Derogation’ principle relating to the full cost recovery requirement in regulation 5(2).

In the introduction table, regulation 6(4)-(6) of the 2010 Regulations, on principles of charging scheme: overriding objective in determining charges, requires a LA to prepare and publish a financial statement, approved by a person with the necessary financial authority, not more than six months after the end of each financial year setting out the chargeable costs, income and any surplus income or deficit arising; the main changes from the 1998 Regulations are that a similar requirement for annual financial statement was set out in regulation 5(6), and there is a new requirement for any surplus income or deficit to be set out in the financial statement, and for the statement to be signed by a person with the necessary financial authority.

In the introduction table, regulation 6(7)-(9) of the 2010 Regulations, on principles of charging scheme: overriding objective in determining charges, says that where a LA first introduces a charging scheme under the 2010 Regulations midway through the financial year, the LA is required to take account of any estimated surplus or deficit arising for that part of the year under the 1998 Regulations, and that reference to “a financial year” is also defined; the main change from the 1998 Regulations is: New provisions.

rows: NOTICE OF WITHDRAWAL OF APPROVAL OF DOCUMENTS GIVING PRACTICAL GUIDANCE WITH RESPECT TO THE REQUIREMENTS OF THE BUILDING REGULATIONS 2010

The Secretary of State hereby gives notice under section 6 of the Building Act 1984 that, in the exercise of the powers under section 6(5), the Secretary of State has withdrawn approval of the documents listed below for the purposes of giving practical guidance with respect to the specified requirements of the Building Regulations 2010. rows: Interpretation: Definition of “controlled service or fitting” is extended to include electrical installations
Interpretation: New definitions are inserted for “electrical installation”, “extra-low voltage” and “low voltage”

Meaning of building work: Part P is added so that the limitation on the definition of building work in relation to the provision of certain Part L1 controlled services or fittings in existing dwellings does not apply to Part P
Requirements relating to material change of use: Part P is added so that, when relevant, work in connection with a material change of use must comply with the technical requirements in Part P
Limitation on requirements: Part P is added so that compliance with Part P does not require anything to be done beyond what is necessary to secure reasonable standards of health and safety
Exempt buildings and work: A paragraph is added so that Part P applies to electrical installations in greenhouses and any small detached building

Giving of a building notice or deposit of plans: Regulation 12(5) is changed so that a person is not required to give a building notice or deposit full plans if (a) registered with one of the self-certification schemes listed in the extended Schedule 2A and intending to carry out building work applicable to that scheme, or (b) intending to carry out electrical work of the nature described in the new Schedule 2B
